webLinks.linkText: Mother's Day Classic Fun Run & Walk 2025

properties.publicTransport: Routes 441, 504 and 506 will be diverting while road closures are in place. Visit transportnsw.info to plan your trip.
properties.otherAdvice:
Thousands of participants will take part in the 5km and 10km Mother's Day Classic fun run and walk events starting from 7am in The Domain. Participants will travel along sections of Macquarie St, College St then Art Gallery Rd and Mrs Macquarie's Rd to finish back in The Domain by approximately 12pm.

Mother's Day is traditionally one of the busiest days on the roads. Wherever you are travelling, expect it to take longer than usual and factor in extra travel time. 

ROAD CLOSURES

  • 5am to 12pm midday: Art Gallery Rd/Mrs Macquarie's Rd from Prince Albert Rd. 
  • 5am to 10.30am: Hospital Rd and a section of Prince Albert Rd. Access to Sydney Hospital and Hospital Rd is via Shakespeare Pl only in both directions.
  • 6am to 10.30am: Macquarie St between St James Rd and Hunter St, College St between Park St and Prince Albert Rd and sections of St James Rd, Prince Albert Rd, St Mary's Rd and Yurong Pkwy will be closed.

Special event clearways will be in effect from 5am to 10.30am on sections of Macquarie St, Hunter St, College St, Prince Albert Rd, St Mary's Rd and St James Rd. Clearways will also be in effect on sections of Prince Albert Rd and Hospital Rd from 5am to 12pm midday.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

During the event hours of 4am to 5pm, motorists will need to allow additional travel time.

Northbound motorists wanting to access Telegraph Point will detour via:

properties.publicTransport: Trains will not drop off at Circular Quay from 6pm-11pm on Saturdays + Sun 8 Jun. Buses will relocate to Martin Place from 6pm Fridays and 5pm on weekends. Light rail will not run between Circular Quay and Town Hall from 6pm Fridays and 5pm on weekends. Ferries will be busy on weekends and access to wharves at Circular Quay will be different on busy nights – follow signage. For more details and top tips to plan your trip, visit transportnsw.info.
properties.otherAdvice:
Vivid Sydney returns for its 15th year for 23 consecutive nights from Friday 23 May to Saturday 14 June and will be lighting up 5 key zones across the city.

The city is no place for cars with road closures and clearway parking restrictions in place each night in Circular Quay, The Rocks, Dawes Point, Millers Point and Ultimo between 3pm and midnight daily, and until 1am on Saturday nights.

Road closures:

  • On Monday to Thursdays: from 3pm local roads in The Rocks, Millers Point and Dawes Point will close including sections of Lower Fort St, Merriman St and Rodens Ln. From 5pm additional roads will close including sections of George St, Argyle St, Harrington St, Pottinger St and Loftus St.
  • On Fridays: additional closures will be in place from 3pm on High St, High Ln, Argyle Pl. From 5pm additional closures will be in place including all of Argyle St, and sections of Hickson Rd, George St, Essex St, Upper Fort St and Watson Rd. From 6pm roads in Circular Quay including Pitt, Loftus, Young, Albert and Phillip Streets will close as well as a section of Darling Dr in Ultimo. From 7pm lanes will close on Erskine St westbound and Kent St southbound.
  • On Saturdays: local closures will be in place from 3pm, and mentioned key roads in Circular Quay, The Rocks, Millers Point, Dawes Point and Ultimo will close from 5pm. Additionally Grosvenor St/Bridge St between York St and Loftus St will be closed - no east/west access via Bridge St during this time. Roads remain closed until 1am on Saturdays. Wheat Rd will close from 7pm to 11pm.
  • On Sundays: local closures will be in place from 3pm, and key roads in Circular Quay, The Rocks, Millers Point, Dawes Point and Ultimo will close from 5pm to midnight.
  • 2pm Friday to 1am Monday: each weekend, George St will close between Lower Fort St and Hickson Rd for The Rocks markets. 

Special event clearways will be in effect on various roads between 3pm and midnight each day during Vivid Sydney on most major roads in the Sydney CBD, The Rocks, Circular Quay, Dawes Point and Haymarket. Some clearways will be in effect earlier from 1pm and 2pm on local roads.

Clearways are strict no-parking zones for all vehicle types, and apply even to local residents and TfNSW Mobility Scheme Permit holders. Check signs carefully as vehicles left in clearways will be towed and a fee applies. If your vehicle is towed, you can search your vehicle registration at the Find My Car website to find its new location, or alternatively call 132 701 to speak to an operator.

properties.publicTransport: Buses will be diverting around closures from 9:30pm to 10pm. Match tickets include travel on transport. Visit transportnsw.info to plan your trip.
properties.otherAdvice:
A-League Men Elimination Final: Western Sydney Wanderers v Melbourne Victory at CommBank Stadium. Kick off at 7:35pm, finishing around 9:30pm.

Traffic will be heavy on roads approaching and within Parramatta as fans travel to and from the game. Allow extra travel time on Parramatta Rd, Church St, Victoria Rd, James Ruse Dr and Pennant Hills Rd.

Road closures

Roads around the stadium will close from 9.30pm until 10pm to allow crowds to safely leave the venue. Roads will re-open once crowds have cleared the area. Closure timings may be extended at short notice subject to extra time and/or penalties.

  • O’Connell Street from Grose Street to George Street 
  • Ross Street from O’Connell Street to Trott Street 
  • Victoria Road from O’Connell Street to Villiers Street 

While closures are in place motorists are encouraged to avoid driving through Parramatta CBD and detour around the closures via Grose Street, Brickfield Street, Victoria Road and Wilde Avenue in both directions.

Roads on approach to the stadium may be temporarily closed as crowds make their way to the game. 

Motorists should also exercise caution as pedestrian activity will be high on roads between Parramatta Interchange and the stadium. 

Be patient leaving car parks as traffic will be heavy and follow the directions of traffic controllers and Police.
